stem: The diagram shows Gopal's paper arrow with a possible vertical mid-line drawn as a dashed fold line.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides when that mid-line is a line of symmetry?

options.text: When folding along the mid-line makes the two parts overlap exactly point for point.
When the two halves look roughly similar from a distance, even if they are never folded.
The mid-line is a line of symmetry for any paper arrow, even when the fold test is never tried.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A line of symmetry requires the exact fold-overlap test along that mid-line.

teacher.key_rationale: Only exact fold-overlap decides a line of symmetry. Looking roughly balanced or assuming any arrow works omits the fold test.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right-triangle tikz into a paper arrow with dashed vertical fold line.
